clue.text: Cutting lover's head in half causes terrible pain

indicators.note: to cut something is to reduce it, so one letter is replaced by a smaller value

blocks.note: the head of the lover is M, Roman 1000; half of that is 500, Roman D
a mistress is a lover; the opening M is the part that gets swapped

explanation.surface: A rejected suitor imagines a violent attack on a sweetheart that would cause dreadful suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: MISTRESS has M at its head; treating M as Roman 1000 and halving it gives D (500), so DISTRESS replaces the M. 'Cutting' and 'in half' sound gruesome but are arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is severe suffering or anguish, a close synonym for agony or great hurt.

clue.text: Protest singers led by Conservative politicians

blocks.note: a demo is a protest march
C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative
an informer 'sings' to the police, and such people are rats

explanation.surface: Folk singers at a protest are fronted by right-wing politicians, an unlikely political rally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singers' looks musical but means informers, people who sing to the police. 'Led by' puts the Conservative ahead of them; the protest comes first in the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Democrats are members of a political party, chiefly the American one, so they are a kind of political figure.

clue.text: Tweeter talks informally about dispute

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to rap is to chat casually
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone posting on social media chats casually about an argument online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tweeter' suggests a social media user, but it means a bird that tweets.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparrow is a small songbird, and birds chirp, so a tweeter is a playful name for one.

clue.text: Broadcaster spoke out, initially ignoring America

indicators.note: to ignore something is to pay it no attention, so those letters are dropped
initially points to the start of a word, so only its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: a spoke of a wheel is a radius
US is the usual short form for America
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A presenter speaks frankly about something, without mentioning America at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoke out' reads as a verb phrase, but 'spoke' is a noun (a wheel's radius) and 'out' only lends its first letter. RADIUS loses US, then O is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio is a device or medium that transmits programmes, so it is a broadcasting outlet.

clue.text: Characteristic of service force

blocks.note: first meaning: a good quality
second meaning: the number of personnel in a military unit

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a feature of good service; 'of' only joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A strength is an asset or merit, and a regiment's strength is its full complement of troops.

clue.text: Spot male priest taking mass outside

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
P is an abbreviation for priest
a pile is a mass or heap; 'outside' says it goes around the rest

explanation.surface: Someone notices a male cleric holding Mass in the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like the church service, but here it is a heap, PILE, wrapped around M and P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimple is a small inflamed blemish on the skin, the same thing as a zit.

clue.text: Series going into quite miserable detail

indicators.note: a run of letters going into the next words sits across them, so the solution is a consecutive string

blocks.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A television series dives into the grim specifics of something rather depressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Series' looks like a TV show, but it is the run of letters inside 'quite miserable'.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to list point by point, so the verb sense of detail matches exactly.

clue.text: Quietly slaughtered five centrally involved in espionage

indicators.note: the central five letters of a word are kept and the outer ones dropped
something slaughtered is torn apart, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the middle five letters of the nine

explanation.surface: Five people involved in spying were silently killed, like a thriller plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Five' looks like a number of victims but counts letters taken from the middle of espionage.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano is the musical direction to play softly, so in a score it means at low volume.

clue.text: This Roman cardinal appears in letter to the Corinthians

definitions.text: This Roman cardinal appears in letter to the Corinthians

blocks.clueFragment: This Roman cardinal appears in letter to the Corinthians
blocks.note: surface reading: a cardinal of the Roman church is named in St Paul's epistle
setter's reading: a cardinal number written as Roman numerals, XI, which is also a letter of the Greek alphabet the Corinthians used

explanation.surface: A senior Catholic churchman is mentioned in Paul's biblical letter to Corinth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' is a cardinal number, not a churchman; 'letter' is an alphabet letter, not an epistle. XI does both jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: XI is the Roman numeral for the number after ten, and xi is the fourteenth Greek letter.

clue.text: Wound king in wicked action

indicators.note: in places one piece within another

blocks.note: mean is nasty or unkind
a deed is an act
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king is injured in a cruel act of violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' looks like an injury, but it is the past tense of wind, rhyming with found.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to follow a twisting course, so a path that meandered snaked about.

clue.text: Foolish person's puzzling use of words

blocks.note: first meaning: an idiot, an informal insult
second meaning: a picture puzzle in which word placement represents a phrase

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possessive, but it stands for 'is', joining two meanings. Dingbats were a popular British puzzle board game of visual word riddles.
explanation.definitionFit: Dingbat is slang for a silly fool and also names a rebus-style word puzzle.

clue.text: Electron beams reportedly destroy recording on tape

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: E is the symbol for an electron, and beams are rays

explanation.surface: Beams of electrons are said to wipe out a tape recording, plausible technical lore.
explanation.walkthrough: E rays said out loud is exactly the verb; the scientific surface hides a simple pun.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase a tape is to wipe its magnetic content, removing what was stored on it.

clue.text: Box office's opening interrupts funny sketch

indicators.note: an opening is a beginning, so only the first letter is taken
to interrupt is to break into, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: a carton is a cardboard box
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: The opening of a theatre box office breaks into a comic stage routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box office' reads as one theatre term, but Box is the carton and office only gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoon is a humorous drawing, and a sketch can mean a drawing as well as a comic scene.

clue.text: Unpleasant gang of criminals briefly returned to infiltrate racket

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the final letter is dropped
returned means sent back, so the letters run the other way
infiltrating means getting inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: a racket is a din
a mob is a criminal gang

explanation.surface: A nasty gang returns briefly to take over a criminal racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' suggests a criminal scheme to match the gang, but here it means noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or disgusting, especially of smells; it has nothing to do with noise.

clue.text: Location of dam and entrance to animal pen?

indicators.note: an entrance is the way in, so the first letter is taken

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A farmyard puzzle: where are the mother animal and the way into its enclosure?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dam' and 'pen' both look farmyard (a mother animal, an enclosure), but the dam is a barrage and the pen is a swan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aswan High Dam spans the Nile in southern Egypt, so the town is where the dam stands.

clue.text: International court blocks country in the blink of an eye

indicators.note: to block is to sit in the way, so one piece lodges inside another

blocks.note: a nation is a country
I is the abbreviation for International
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A world court suddenly obstructs a nation, all in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'International court' looks like a single body, but it splits into I and CT; 'in the' is part of the definition phrase rather than a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nictation is the technical word for winking or blinking, so it names the eyelid's quick closing.

clue.text: Part of play that's still contributing to respectable audience

indicators.note: letters that contribute to a phrase form part of it, so the solution lies inside the words

blocks.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A quiet moment in a stage play is helping please a well-behaved theatre crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as an adverb (yet) but is the adjective motionless, belonging to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a motionless scene arranged on stage, the actors frozen in a picture.

clue.text: Successful period for every state capital

blocks.note: an up, as in ups and downs, is a good spell
per means for each
a case is a state of affairs

explanation.surface: A good spell for each US state's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State capital' reads as a city like Albany, but capital is the definition and means a capital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppercase letters are capitals, named from the top typesetting tray where printers kept them.

clue.text: Firm retains most beneficial item under pressure

indicators.note: most of something is not all of it, so the final letter is lost
to retain is to keep hold of, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: hard means firm
an asset is something useful

explanation.surface: A company keeps hold of its best assets while under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company, but it is the adjective hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone harassed is stressed and hounded by demands, the same as feeling hard-pressed.

clue.text: Small fish? One hopes it's not smelt

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Is this a little fish? Hopefully not a smelt, which is a kind of small fish.
explanation.walkthrough: A smelt is itself a small fish, so the definition seems to continue the fishy theme; really smelt is the past participle of smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a foul odour, which anyone would rather not have to breathe in.

clue.text: What Car? regularly takes up issue with those that listen

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
in a down entry, up means read from the bottom, so the order is turned round

blocks.note: eh? is an informal way to say what?
taken as written
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: What Car?, the British motoring magazine, often complains about something to do with listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic title tempts you to read the magazine name as one unit, but its two words do separate jobs; eh? is a casual way of asking what?, and 'regularly' applies only to 'takes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ears are the organs that hear, and a pain in them is a medical problem with your hearing apparatus.

clue.text: Sort of opiate inspiring welcome state

indicators.note: to sort is to rearrange, so these letters are put in a new order
inspiring literally means breathing in, so one piece is drawn inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A kind of narcotic produces a pleasant, welcome state of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a frame of mind induced by the drug, but it is a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethiopia is a sovereign country in the Horn of Africa, and a nation is a state.

clue.text: Provider of cover belonging to person taking action to preserve right

indicators.note: to preserve something is to keep it safe within, so one piece is held by another

blocks.note: to be in a group is to belong to it
someone who takes legal action sues
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A cover provider belongs to someone suing to protect their rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking action' sounds like doing something, but it is legal action, so the person is a litigant.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurer is a company that underwrites policies, giving financial protection against loss.

clue.text: Raised note beginning to reinforce echo effect

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept
in a down entry, raising something brings its bottom to the top, turning the order round

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
a breve is a long musical note

explanation.surface: A musician raises a note at the start to boost the echo, studio talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical surface fits the answer, so 'note' reads naturally; a breve is a long note worth two whole notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverb, short for reverberation, is the sound processing that adds a lingering echo.

clue.text: Enduring impression finally captured by a French painter

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the last letter is kept
something captured is held inside, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: per means a, as in five pounds a head
Edouard Manet was a French painter
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A lasting impression is captured by a French Impressionist painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impression' hints at Impressionism, which suits Manet, but supplies only its last letter; 'a' is PER, as in so much a day.
explanation.definitionFit: Something permanent lasts indefinitely, so it is lasting in the same sense as enduring.

clue.text: Implores Francophone country to suppress resistance

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down within, so one piece is kept inside another

blocks.note: pays is the French for country
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone begs a French-speaking nation to crush an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Francophone country' looks like Belgium or Senegal, but it means the country word in French.
explanation.definitionFit: To pray in the old sense is to beg earnestly, as in 'pray tell', so it equals begs.

clue.text: Ends year on a bit of a high?

definitions.text: on a bit of a high?

blocks.note: the tips of things are their ends
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Someone finishes the year on a happy note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ends' looks like a verb, but it is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipsy means slightly drunk, and mild drunkenness is a light, merry high.

clue.text: Runs into drunk American rather carelessly

indicators.note: going into something means entering it, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: a sot is a drunkard
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Someone bumps into an intoxicated American in a fairly careless way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carelessly' belongs to the definition: it tells you the answer is the slurred, casual form of 'sort of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorta is informal spelling of 'sort of', meaning somewhat, the way people say it casually.

clue.text: Vault yields missing case in public records

indicators.note: a case is the outside, so without it the first and last letters are removed

blocks.note: a vault is an arched roof
to yield is to give

explanation.surface: A bank vault gives up a lost court case buried in official files.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vault' suggests a strongroom for records, but it is the architectural arch; 'case' is the outer letters, not a legal case.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a collection of historical documents, often kept by governments, so it holds official files.

clue.text: Drain clogged with hair repelled unpopular people

indicators.note: a clogged pipe is blocked by something inside it, so one piece is held within another
to repel is to drive back, so the letters go backwards

blocks.note: to sap is to drain energy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plughole blocked with hair disgusts people, a grim bathroom scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drain' looks like a plughole, but it is the verb sap; 'repelled' reads as disgusted but signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pariahs are outcasts shunned by society, so they are people nobody wants around.

clue.text: Polish husband's dated clothing

indicators.note: clothing covers a body, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: people who are seeing each other are dating
H is the abbreviation for husband; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A Polish man's outfit is old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with its capital looks like the nationality but means shine; 'dated' looks like old-fashioned but means went out with.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheen is a soft gloss on a surface, the shine that polishing produces.

clue.text: Object of desire developed finer body

indicators.note: something developed has been worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone longed for has worked out and built a better physique.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface itself reads like a description of an attractive partner, which helps hide the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A boyfriend is a romantic partner, someone you are attracted to and want to be with.
